:::{#exm-bayes}
#### Positive predictive value of a medical test

Suppose a disease test has 99% sensitivity and 99% specificity,
and the prevalence of the disease in the population is 7%.

Let $D$ be the event "person has the disease"
and $\posclass$ be the event "test is positive".
Then:

- $\Pr(\posclass \mid D) = 0.99$ (sensitivity)
- $\Pr(\negclass \mid \neg D) = 0.99$ (specificity),
  so the false positive rate is

  $$
  \begin{aligned}
  \Pr(\posclass \mid \neg D) &= 1 - 0.99 \\
  &= 0.01
  \end{aligned}
  $$

- $\Pr(D) = 0.07$ (prevalence)

By @thm-bayes, with the denominator expanded by the
[law of total probability](#thm-total-prob-conditional) over the
[partition](#def-partition) $\{D, \neg D\}$:

$$
\ba
\Pr(D \mid \posclass)
&= \frac{\Pr(\posclass \mid D) \cd \Pr(D)}{\Pr(\posclass)}
&& \text{(Bayes' theorem)} \\
&= \frac{\Pr(\posclass \mid D) \cd \Pr(D)}{\Pr(\posclass \mid D) \cd \Pr(D) + \Pr(\posclass \mid \neg D) \cd \Pr(\neg D)}
&& \text{(law of total probability)} \\
&= \frac{0.99 \cd 0.07}{0.99 \cd 0.07 + 0.01 \cd 0.93}
&& \text{(substitute the given values)} \\
&= \frac{0.0693}{0.0693 + 0.0093}
&& \text{(multiply each term in the numerator and denominator)} \\
&= \frac{0.0693}{0.0786}
&& \text{(add the denominator's two terms)} \\
&\approx 0.88
&& \text{(divide)}
\ea
$$

Even with a highly accurate test (99% sensitive and 99% specific),
only about 88% of people who test positive actually have the disease,
because the disease prevalence is relatively low (7%).

:::
